sets.title: Feminine and Neuter
sets.description: Practice accusative adjective endings for feminine and neuter nouns
sets.descriptionRussian: Окончания прилагательных в винительном падеже: женский и средний род

items.prompt: Я купила _____ юбку. (I bought a new skirt.)
Мы видим _____ озеро. (We see a big lake.)
items.explanation: Neuter accusative = nominative: большое stays большое.

items.prompt: Она читает _____ газету. (She reads the morning newspaper.)
Он пьёт _____ молоко. (He drinks warm milk.)

minimalPairs.context: _____ книга лежит на столе. (An interesting book is on the table.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: An interesting book is on the table. (subject = nominative)

minimalPairs.context: Я читаю _____ книгу. (I'm reading an interesting book.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I'm reading an interesting book. (object = accusative)

blanks: Она носит _____ платье. (She wears a red dress.)
Мы слушаем _____ музыку. (We listen to Russian music.)
Он открыл _____ окно. (He opened the old window.)

sets.title: Animate Masculine Trap
sets.description: The hardest part: animate masculine accusative = genitive ending
sets.descriptionRussian: Самое сложное: одушевлённый мужской род = окончание родительного

items.prompt: Я вижу _____ студента. (I see a new student.) - animate
items.promptEnglish: I see a new student. (animate masculine)
items.explanation: Animate masculine: новый → нового (-ый → -ого, like genitive).

items.prompt: Он купил _____ телефон. (He bought a new phone.) - inanimate
items.promptEnglish: He bought a new phone. (inanimate masculine)
items.explanation: Inanimate masculine: accusative = nominative. Новый stays новый.

items.prompt: Мы встретили _____ соседа. (We met an old neighbor.) - animate
Она нашла _____ ключ. (She found an old key.) - inanimate
items.explanation: Inanimate masculine: accusative = nominative. Старый ключ.

patternRecognition.sentence: Вижу нового студента. vs. Купил новый телефон.
patternRecognition.question: Why is the adjective different in these accusative sentences?
options: Студент is animate (person), so the adjective takes genitive form. Телефон is inanimate, so it stays nominative.
One is past tense, one is present
patternRecognition.answer: Студент is animate (person), so the adjective takes genitive form. Телефон is inanimate, so it stays nominative.
patternRecognition.explanation: The animate/inanimate distinction only matters for masculine accusative. Animate = genitive endings (-ого), inanimate = nominative endings (-ый).

errorCorrection.hint: Animate masculine accusative needs genitive form for both noun and adjective.
errorCorrection.explanation: Animate masculine: врач → врача (noun), молодой → молодого (adjective). Both change.

errorCorrection.hint: Language is inanimate, so accusative = nominative.
errorCorrection.explanation: Язык is inanimate: accusative = nominative. Русский язык, not русского языка.
Animate: учитель → учителя. The adjective should also change: хорошего учителя.

sets.title: All Genders Mixed
sets.description: Practice accusative adjectives across all genders in the same set
sets.descriptionRussian: Прилагательные в винительном падеже всех родов

items.prompt: Она выбрала _____ сумку. (She chose a beautiful bag.)
Мы встретили _____ друга. (We met a good friend.)
Я вижу _____ здание. (I see a tall building.)

translation.hint: Animate masculine: младший → младшего, брат → брата

sets.title: Plural Accusative
sets.description: Accusative adjective endings in plural (animate vs inanimate)
sets.descriptionRussian: Окончания прилагательных множественного числа в винительном

items.prompt: Я читаю _____ книги. (I'm reading interesting books.) - inanimate plural
items.explanation: Inanimate plural: accusative = nominative. Интересные книги.

items.prompt: Мы знаем _____ людей. (We know interesting people.) - animate plural
items.explanation: Animate plural: accusative = genitive. Интересных людей.

items.prompt: Она купила _____ цветы. (She bought beautiful flowers.) - inanimate plural
items.hint: Flowers are inanimate: plural accusative = nominative.

minimalPairs.context: Я вижу _____ дома. (I see new houses.)
minimalPairs.explanation: Inanimate plural: accusative = nominative. Новые дома.

minimalPairs.context: Я вижу _____ студентов. (I see new students.)
minimalPairs.explanation: Animate plural: accusative = genitive. Новых студентов.

blanks: Мы пригласили _____ друзей. (We invited old friends.)
Они строят _____ здания. (They're building new buildings.)
Я встретил _____ девушек. (I met beautiful girls.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Animate plural = genitive, inanimate plural = nominative
hints: Friends are animate: plural accusative = genitive.
Buildings are inanimate: plural accusative = nominative.
Girls are animate: plural accusative = genitive.

sets.title: Mixed Challenge
sets.description: All accusative adjective patterns in one round
sets.descriptionRussian: Все правила прилагательных в винительном падеже

items.prompt: Дети любят _____ собаку. (The children love the big dog.)
items.promptEnglish: The children love the big dog.
items.explanation: Feminine: большая → большую. (Собака is grammatically feminine even if the dog is male.)

items.prompt: Он смотрит _____ фильм. (He's watching a funny movie.)
items.hint: Film is inanimate masculine: accusative = nominative.

items.prompt: Врач осмотрел _____ ребёнка. (The doctor examined the sick child.)
items.promptEnglish: The doctor examined the sick child.

errorCorrection.explanation: Feminine accusative: интересная → интересную. (Передача → передачу too.)

errorCorrection.hint: The adjective is correct (animate masculine), but the noun also needs accusative.
errorCorrection.explanation: Both must be accusative: маленького котёнка. The noun was left in nominative.
